sentences.english_text: There were direct telephone lines to Japan, England, France, and Italy.
And officers were speaking on, warning their allies that something terrible was happening.
The problem was that they were not sure just what.
Are you sure it's a Russian attack?
The Japanese ambassador asked.
No it could be China or India or Albania.
The computers keep telling us different things.
The computers were trying to stop sending out mixed up messages.
But they had to do what the master computer ordered.
And the master computer was unable to function properly because Drippy was inside it.
And what was Drippy doing during all this excitement?
He was sound asleep, dreaming about riding on the tail of the wind, having hundreds of people bowing to him, and being applauded as a famous stage star.
The president of the United States arrived at the war room.
And when he saw how crazily all the computers were acting, he said, This is very serious.
I think we're being attacked.
Launch your planes with the missiles.
We've got to strike Russia before Russia strikes us.
Yes, Mr. President.
A general picked up the telephone and said, Group A, launch your planes immediately.
And he put the telephone down and said, They'll be in the air within three minutes, Mr. President, on their way to bomb Russia.
The president looked very grave.
I never thought the Russians would attack us.
This means World War III.
I know, sir.
And all the men in the room were very solemn.
